main_body: Snow-roofed stone well: a snow-covered roof on two wooden posts above a round stone well with a dark opening and a stone base course
top_band: At x=15, the pale snow roof (L 166-249) runs rows 2-8. Lower down, the well rim and opening ellipse (rows 16-23) read as the horizontal surface of the well body.
evidence: The well body shows a light rim at row 16, then a dark ellipse of water and shadow (rows 17-22) with a brown bucket or rope block inside, then a lighter front rim line at row 23 (L=145). Rows 24-30 form a stone front face with dark mortar bands, and the dark rows 24-26 under the rim act as the eave shadow. The opening is a real ellipse that can be seen into, not a line across the rim. The snow roof also reads as a wide lighter top surface with a front edge and icicles. Both parts follow the 3/4 contract, so it matches the roofed-well reference.

style.evidence: The snow has about 5 steps (white, pale blue, mid blue-grey, dark blue). The wood posts have a light-to-dark brown ramp, and the stone has several greys with mortar bands. The measured facts support this: 0% flat-fill coverage and 0% neutral dark edge pixels, so the outlines carry a tint. At 14 colours per tile and 24 distinct colours it is somewhat below the references (17-20 per tile, 38-40 distinct) but still information-rich, and it sits acceptably next to the roofed-well reference.
